questions.question:
Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as the two numbers of the pair given below.

20 : 68
If the signs - and ÷ are interchanged, then which of the following equations would be correct?
questions.solution:
**__BODMAS RULE:__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebadc30a979bf1a7e953d20901c3e7953c575296c0e0bb4af8a458ec3a64ab2c.png] 

On Checking and Interchanged each option one by one:

1) 12 + 4 - 4 ÷ 2 = 3

By interchanging - and ÷ in the given equations.

Interchanged equation is: 12 + __**4 ÷ 4**__ - 2 = 3

⇒ __**12 + 1**__ - 2 = 3

⇒ __**13 - 2**__ = 3

⇒ 11 ≠ 3

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

2) 6 ÷ 3 + 12 - 6 = 5

**By interchanging - and ÷ in the given equations.**

**Interchanged equation is: 6 - 3 + __12 ÷ 6 __= 5 **

**⇒ __6__ - 3 __+ 2__ = 5**

**⇒ __8 - 3__ = 5**

**⇒ 5 = 5**

**⇒ LHS = RHS**

3) 12 ÷ 3 + 9 - 9 = 4

By interchanging - and ÷ in the given equations.

Interchanged equations is: 12 - 3 + __**9 ÷ 9**__ = 4

⇒ __**12 **__- 3 __**+ 1**__ = 4

⇒ **__13 - 3__** = 4

⇒ 10 ≠ 4 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

4) 9 ÷ 9 - 9 + 9 = 9

By interchanging - and ÷ in the given equations.

Interchanged equations is: 9 - __**9 ÷ 9**__ + 9 = 9

⇒ __**9 **__- 1 __**+ 9 **__= 9

⇒ **__18 - 1__** = 9 

⇒ 17 ≠ 9

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: If MARKET is coded as 15 and SUBMARINE is coded as 21, then how would CONVENTIONAL be coded?
questions.solution:
**Logic: [Number of letters × 2 + 3] **

'MARKET' is coded as '15'

Number of letter in MARKET = 6

→ __**6 × 2**__ + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15

'SUBMARINE' is coded as '21'

Number of letter in SUBMARINE = 9

→ __**9 × 2**__ + 3 = 18 + 3 = 21

Similarly,

**'CONVENTIONAL' **is coded as **'?'**

Number of letter in CONVENTIONAL = 12

→ __**12 × 2**__ + 3 = 24 + 3 =** 27**

Hence, the correct answer is **"27".**

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U read a magazine one after another.

i. S was neither the first nor the last to read it.

ii. There were as many readers between P and T as there were between R and P.

iii. S read it sometime before Q, who read it sometime after U.

iv. The one who read it last had taken it from R.

Who were the two persons to have read the magazine first and last, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

Six persons: P, Q, R, S, U and T.

**1. The one who read it last had taken it from R**.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/858606a14fbce32d0d80df1c53a2d288fb97ca391d96e4314a82a3aa3cde8768.png] 

As R read the magazine before the Last one it means R read the magazine.

**2. S was neither the first nor the last to read it**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9018de3e7afb6396f439ec1197ba8886b1dc6659bc3cd74419858a327b69bc9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ff118e923a1bdc9428771b13f2a63ca2480f00667f9e19554449320b86baf5a.png] ** **

As S was neither the first nor the last to read the magazine, S was read the magazine on the 2ⁿd or 3rd , or 4th number.so there are three cases.

**3. S read it sometime before Q, who read it sometime after U**

​There are 4 cases showing the reading number of 'Q' with respect to 'S'.

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78fbef07db9e847766f84994340aed741b3a356f22ecb49e3afc9ecd6bdfe413.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b8f164295f8a1b4970c5559981cb3597e559b6ec7cceb30349e8eae72f6e3b3.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21536a54b18774c52975628fa85eabea84724d8e203461f6e75d4f068c6a68a8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff290da3b771a731d8dadd933d43396ea954cf6369dae4dd94e463dd08f708c8.png] 

There are 7 cases showing the reading number of 'Q' with respect to 'U'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/550174cc9e927c1a5e129ac8ccd269580b6448e204fdfbc6c9d63646c306a7e3.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7126eb43acf6c280f1077a9d98dfd06fba701c8a883ef9144f7630026ebe7e2c.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f11ee461895dde0aee72d7e4c66012627bea6b34a74aa76e866609a7b88f51a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86247238e8143d55e8d54d6b24a07db329267fa06f33ec1ec8d79219e9102c34.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aae874e6bd245c30b4db914108e189f0ef503bdb3cf68169c3c7b602e1d86098.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50eb204c510d01009bbe64ff55bfe8277146371c1a986b82e9bce123a1785c1d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aff579ba6f1b4defbd0d9f68ed3d94985b0e0fc93e24ae795a1c1438cb70dec7.png] 

**4. ****There were as many readers between P and T as there were between R and P**.

​So,​according to this statement, all the above 6 cases are eliminated only one case (case-2) remaining that shows the sequence of reading the magazine by all 6 persons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf9d3cc136f53b1089e103638d63b314813dc453469a88a222427cdbb5a9e4fe.png] 

As per the above statement, we can say that number of readers between P and T is equal to the number of readers between R and P. here Between T and P only one reader which is U. similarly, between P and R only one reader which is S.

Thus, T and Q have read the magazine first and last respectively.

Hence, The correct answer is "T and Q".

questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

Statements:

1. All buildings are shops.

2. Some shops are boutiques.

3. No restaurant is a boutique.

Conclusions:

I. Some boutiques are buildings.

II. Some restaurants being buildings is a possibility.

III. No restaurant is a shop.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
__**Least Possible Venn diagrams**__:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74aecdcdcb9662d8e048c097360fe37ecf777adde80fbba91d1fd7c4c825abb7.png] 

**Conclusions: **

**I. **Some boutiques are buildings → **Doesn't Follow **(As some shops are boutiques and all buildings are shops, so we can not say anything definite about some boutiques are building.it is a possibility)

This possibility scenario can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30e507f08836ffcbe3eb949dca0c27d5d8b9a053243b7810389ba3cb3c0a3fbf.png] 

Here, No boutique is a building. that is why this statement is a possibility. 

**II. **Some restaurants being buildings is a possibility →** Follow **(As no restaurant is a boutique , some boutique are shops and all buildings are shops. so we can not say anything about some restaurants are building,** it is a possibility **)

This possibility scenario can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da96a0a9d9a34cc06c83b198e2670e84e9822ab7669f8072680cd3c22b8cd235.png] 

Here, some buildings are restaurants that's why this given possibility is followed.

**III**. No restaurant is a shop → **Doesn't Follow **(As some boutiques are shops and no boutique is a restaurant, so Some part of restaurant is not shop, but No restaurant is a shop can be possible only)

Thus, **Only conclusion II follows**.

Hence,** **the correct answer is " Only conclusion II follows".

questions.question: If FRIEND is coded as 86 and SICK is coded as 62, then how would FRECKLE be coded?
questions.solution:
Table shows the positional value of alphabets.

__**Logic**__: **Sum of positional value + (Number of letters × 10) ÷ 2**

**⇒ F + R + I + E + N + D**

⇒ 6 + 18 + 9 + 5 + 14 + 4 = 56

⇒ 6 Alphabet = 10 × 6 = 60

⇒ 60 ÷ 2 = 30

⇒ 56 + 30 = **86**
